title: Tenant SLOs-backed soft-stop and resume protocol for limiter outages
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design and implement a soft-stop + resume protocol for rate limiter outages that respects tenant SLOs and minimizes hard denials during transient limiter failures. The protocol should allow partial serving, proportional shedding, and an automated lease/handshake-based resume so that applications experience graceful degradation rather than hard errors. This complements existing circuit-breaker and quota fallback logic by introducing a short-lived, stateful slowdown mode negotiated between frontends and limiter backends.
acceptance_criteria: When limiter is configured to soft-stop, tenants receive 0 hard 5xx denies for at least 60s after failure onset; requests are either partially served, queued with a bounded wait, or downgraded deterministically.
In chaos test (simulated limiter outage across one region), global multi-region routing reduces cross-region failovers by >30% compared to current emergency fallback baseline.
Fairness: within a 5m window after failover, the relative token share deviation between tenants <= 7% compared to pre-failure baseline for tenants with the same SLO tier.
Resume handshake completes successfully and restores pre-failure throughput within configured ramp window (default 120s) without token overshoot.
End-to-end test coverage and gated feature-flag rollout in console with metrics surfaced (blocked_by, soft_stop_ratio, resume_success_rate).
technical_decisions: Implement soft-stop as an intermediate limiter state: NORMAL -> SOFT_STOP -> DRAIN -> RESUME.
Use lease-based handshake (short-lived leases) between limiter pool leaders and frontend proxies for resume authorization to prevent split-brain rehydration.
Proportional shedding will use exponentially-weighted recent-token-rate per-tenant combined with configured SLO weight to compute a fair share multiplier.
Queueing is bounded and best-effort at frontends; prefer returning streamed partial responses or preemptive throttled responses rather than synchronous 5xx.
Expose telemetry: per-tenant soft_stop_enter_ts, soft_stop_exit_ts, tokens_served_during_soft_stop, and shed_fraction.
Do not rely on global consistent storage during outage; prefer local soft-state with periodic reconciliation once control-plane connectivity returns.
Integrate with existing circuit-breaker thresholds but add a separate path for lease renewal and resume to avoid permanent breakers blocking resume path.
Security: resume handshake signed with instance key; KMS for lease encryption is optional for Dedicated/Private deployments.
Fallback: if resume handshake fails after N attempts, escalate to configured emergency-deny policy and surface alerts to oncall.
Make feature controllable via config flags and per-customer opt-out (enterprise customers may prefer strict denies for compliance).
implementation_steps: Spec: write formal protocol spec and sequence diagrams (Confluence) — owner: Lina (PRD link in links).
Limiter runtime: add SOFT_STOP state machine, lease issuer, and resume validator — owner: Rajiv (ENG-79812-PR1).
Frontend proxy: implement bounded queue + partial-respond semantics and fair-share multiplier logic — owner: Mei (ENG-79812-PR2).
Control plane: feature flags, tenant SLO weight config, and dashboard instrumentation — owner: Priya (ENG-79812-PR3).
E2E tests: unit + integration in local cluster; chaos test harness to simulate partial regional outage — owner: QA team (ENG-79812-TEST).
Canary rollout: region-staged enablement gated by metrics and kill-switch — owner: SRE (runbook linked).
Docs & SDKs: update console feature flag UI and SDK retry helpers to recognize soft-stop signals — owner: DevX.
Post-deploy: monitor soft_stop_ratio, resume_success_rate, fairness_drift, and run retrospective after 2 weeks of canary.
Rollout to Dedicated/Private customers as opt-in with migration guide and KMS recommendations.
Add migration scripts to backfill telemetry for historical analysis.
Create runbook for oncall: detection, mitigation, manual resume flow, and rollback steps.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal dev cluster tests; flag off in all regions.
Stage 1: enable for internal traffic and Redwood test tenants in us-west-2 only; monitor for 48h.
Stage 2: gradual expansion to us-east-1 and eu-west-1 with 10% tenant sampling and automated rollback on alert.
Stage 3: full global enablement for hosteds after 1 week of stable telemetry; Dedicated/Private as opt-in.
All stages require health gates: no increase in P99 errors, <5% increase in average tail-latency, fairness_drift < 10%.
Feature flag: runtime.soft_stop_v2 with per-customer override; emergency kill-switch in Console and SRE tooling.
Canary kill criteria: resume_success_rate < 80% over 30m, or soft_stop_ratio > 30% for >1h for non-test tenants.
testing: Unit tests for state transitions and lease validation (target 95%+ coverage for new modules).
Integration tests: multi-proxy + limiter pool with simulated network partition and leader failover.
Chaos test: region-level limiter outage (single region) to validate multi-region routing and reduced cross-region failovers.
Fairness simulation: synthetic tenants with varying SLO weights to validate proportional shedding math across workloads.
Load test: peak qps with soft-stop enabled to measure tail latency and serviceability under bounded queueing.
Backward compatibility test: clients that don't understand soft-stop should still receive safe retryable responses or clear well-documented error metadata.
Integration with observability: dashboards and alerts wired to new metrics; runbook playthrough by SRE.
